Munich 1972 Olympic pictograms

Otl Aicher’s sport pictograms: figures drawn only with circles and bars on a 45-degree and 90-degree grid.

Source
Wikipedia: Otl Aicher
Creator
Otl Aicher and Abteilung XI für visuelle Gestaltung, Organisationskomitee der XX. Olympischen Spiele München
Made
1972
Style
International Typographic Style (German extension; agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Systematic, clear, friendly, rational
Evidence
Downloaded two CC BY 1.0 photographs by Henning Schlottmann of the pictograms still on site in Munich (swimming hall, Olympiazentrum station) to a scratch folder and inspected them. Poster data read on eMuseum record 230065. No image is stored.
Reviewed
25 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Otl Aicher co-founded and taught at the Ulm School of Design and led the design team of the 1972 Summer Olympics in Munich, overseeing its system of pictograms. Wikipedia: Otl Aicher.

Wikipedia’s history-of-design article quotes Michael Bierut praising the pictograms for their elegance and clarity. Wikipedia: History of graphic design.

The Museum für Gestaltung Zürich holds the poster Piktogramme – München 1972 – Montreal 1976 (concept Otl Aicher; offset, 84 × 59.5 cm, object 33-0114). eMuseum object 230065.

Observed

  • Each sign is a square panel in one flat color (light blue at the swimming hall, green at the station) with a white figure.
  • Heads are plain circles detached from the body; limbs and torsos are straight bars with rounded ends.
  • Bars run only at vertical, horizontal, and 45-degree angles. The runner’s legs and the footballer’s body are built from the same few angles.
  • The football is a white outline circle, the only outlined shape in the two station panels.
  • The panels carry no text.

Why it belongs

The pictograms extend the style from type to symbols: a small set of parts on a fixed geometric grid produces a large family that stays consistent across sports and sites.

Borrow

Build icons from a restricted kit: one circle size, one bar width, and only 0°, 45°, and 90° angles.

Separate the head or key element from the body with a gap so shapes read clearly at small size.

Use one flat background color per zone or category, and white for the symbol.
